sources.entry: Engity's Bifröst - Highly customizable SSH server with several ways to authorize a user and options where and how to execute a user's session. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Go/Docker

summary.one_liner: Bifröst is a configurable SSH server and gateway that lets teams control access to hosts and isolated work environments, with several ways to authorize users and choose where sessions run.
summary.what_it_does: Users connect with a standard SSH client such as OpenSSH or PuTTY, without a Bifröst-specific client. Access flows can authorize users with local accounts, SSH keys, or OIDC Device Authorization, which also requires a browser and a suitable identity provider. A session can run as a local user, in a Docker container, or in a Kubernetes Pod, and managed local accounts can optionally be provisioned and cleaned up. It can act as an SSH gateway to private SSH servers using a separately authenticated connection with target host-key verification. It can optionally write signed audit events and verifiable terminal recordings. OIDC can close connections after a refresh grant is rejected, and connection and session lifetimes can be set for time-bound access.
use_cases: replace an OpenSSH sshd on hosts
give team members SSH access via OIDC login
run user sessions in Docker containers
run user sessions in Kubernetes Pods
how_to_run: Install Bifröst on Linux, Windows or macOS as a host service, or choose a container installation (see the documentation at bifroest.engity.org)
Choose a published release and its matching versioned documentation
Follow a task guide: OIDC login with a standard SSH client, SSH gateway to an OpenSSH server, or verifiable session recording
Select SSH access policies using the configuration reference
notable: Works with standard SSH clients, no custom client needed
Multiple authorization flows: local accounts, SSH keys, OIDC Device Authorization
Session can run as host user, Docker container, or Kubernetes Pod
Signed audit events and verifiable terminal recordings
SSH gateway with target host-key verification
caveats: OIDC Device Authorization requires a browser and a suitable identity provider
Time-bound access behavior should be tested against your IdP and requirements
Container installs of alpha and beta builds use only full version tags; :latest is for stable releases only
